clue.text: Nuts make birds land

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of the two words that follow go mad and rearrange

explanation.surface: Crazy creatures somehow force birds to come down to earth.
explanation.definitionFit: To land from a ship or plane is to get off it and step ashore, a direct synonym.

clue.text: 2nd March release for 4D?

parts.note: a protest march is a demo
B is the second letter, as in a 2nd-class grade marked B

explanation.surface: It reads like a dated note: on the second of March an officer is let go.
explanation.walkthrough: '2nd March' looks like a date, but 'March' is a protest and '2nd' is the letter B. 4D is ARMY OFFICER; the question mark flags that an officer is just one example of someone discharged.
explanation.definitionFit: Demobilisation is the discharge of soldiers from service, so it is the release an army officer gets.

clue.text: Pessimistic prediction of failure of grass salad

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf, grass with its roots
slaw, short for coleslaw, is a cabbage salad

explanation.surface: Someone gloomily forecasts that a salad made of grass will flop.
explanation.walkthrough: SOD'S LAW is the British name for the idea that whatever can go wrong will, much like Murphy's Law.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying holds that anything that can go wrong will, which is a gloomy forecast of things going badly.

clue.text: Coming from Eton, all I'm campaigning about is old boy making it as PM

definitions.text: old boy making it as PM

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the buried letters read backwards
the letters come straight out of the run of words that follows, buried in them

explanation.surface: An old Etonian's campaign speech boasts of an old boy who rose to Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming from' takes NALLIMCAM out of 'Eton, all I'm campaigning', and 'about' turns it round. An 'old boy' is a former pupil of a school, and Eton is a famous English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Macmillan, educated at Eton, was British Prime Minister from 1957 to 1963.

clue.text: Liberal mercy of fair leader of men

indicators.note: liberal means free and loose, so the letters of the next three words are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician pleads for mercy from a just leader of men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like a party name, but it is the anagram signal for MERCY OF FAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A commissioned rank in the army commands soldiers, so its holder leads men.

clue.text: Parking not bad up a terrace

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
okay, OK, means not bad

explanation.surface: Parking spaces beside a football stand's terrace are rated decent.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kop is the famous standing terrace at Liverpool's Anfield stadium; the name is used for similar terraces at other English football grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is given to a steep bank of standing terracing behind a goal at a football ground.

clue.text: Streaker's business to be pursued by police

definitions.note: here the 's stands for is: a streaker is

indicators.note: being pursued means being followed, so the police come after the business

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: A naked streaker's business is to run with the police chasing behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streaker' suggests a naked runner at a sports match, but here it is something that streaks across the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet streaks across the night sky trailing a bright tail, so it is a fanciful streaker.

clue.text: Part of bulb broke in two

definitions.meaning: one of the small segments of a garlic bulb
a past tense of cleave, to split apart

explanation.surface: A flower bulb split down the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A garlic bulb is made of segments with this name, and the old past tense of cleave means split.

clue.text: Educated woman unwrapped small packages for husband and wife

indicators.note: the trimmed word wraps up the woman, holding her inside
unwrapped means the outer letters of the word small are stripped away

parts.note: Rita is the heroine of the play and film Educating Rita

explanation.surface: A learned woman opens little parcels for a married couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwrapped' takes the ends off SMALL to leave MAL, which then 'packages' RITA. Educating Rita is a Willy Russell play and film about a hairdresser studying literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital describes what belongs to marriage, so it is an adjective for something shared by a husband and wife.

clue.text: Adventurous boy ate worms wriggling around yard

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the yard abbreviation
wriggling means squirming about, so the letters of ate worms squirm into a new order

explanation.surface: A daring lad swallowed worms that squirmed all over the yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain's novel follows the escapades of this boy on the Mississippi, a classic young adventurer.

clue.text: A bit of poetry treasured by mother

indicators.note: something treasured is held close, so mother holds it inside

parts.note: mum is mother
odic is the adjective for an ode, a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A scrap of verse is kept dear by a mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of poetry' wants to be an ode as a single piece, but the definition is just 'A bit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A modicum is a small quantity, a little amount of something.

clue.text: List of instructions for school run pocketed

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: pocketed means held inside, so the school holds the run

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A checklist for the morning school run sits tucked away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school run' reads as the daily drive to school, but 'school' is a gam, a group of whales, and 'run' is R.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer program is a set of coded commands for a machine to follow.

clue.text: Food that might be hot or cold from the sea

indicators.note: taking cold from the sea removes that letter

parts.note: the Baltic is a sea of northern Europe
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A dish that may be served hot or chilled, fresh from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot or cold' looks like a pairing of serving temperatures, but 'or' is a link and 'cold' is the letter C taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a curry cooked and served in a metal bowl, and curries are often fiery.

clue.text: Band of gold painter applied to furniture

indicators.note: applied to means stuck on, so the painter is placed against the furniture, after it

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a chest is a piece of furniture
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword painter

explanation.surface: A strip of gilt is painted onto a piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band of gold' reads as a ring or stripe, but 'Band' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large group of musicians playing together, a kind of band.

clue.text: Helpful chap making container for beer, perhaps worried about drip

parts.words: chap making container for beer, perhaps
parts.note: a cooper makes barrels, such as those holding beer

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so worried goes around drip

parts.note: ate is past tense of eat in the sense of worry, as in what's eating you
IV, intravenous, is a medical drip

explanation.surface: A useful brewery hand making a barrel frets over a leak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drip' looks like a leaking barrel, but it is a hospital IV drip.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cooperative works willingly with others, which makes them obliging and of use.

clue.text: Swear Polo has nothing in the middle?

indicators.note: has here means holds, so the car holds the other piece
in the middle says where the held piece sits, between the car's two letters

parts.note: the Polo is a car made by Volkswagen, VW
O, the zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A Polo mint, famous for the hole in its middle, is offered as proof.
explanation.walkthrough: Polo is a British mint sold as 'the mint with the hole', so 'nothing in the middle' seems to describe it; here Polo is the Volkswagen car.
explanation.definitionFit: To vow is to swear a solemn promise.

clue.text: Final bit of surgery ma covets after labour?

definitions.text: Final bit of surgery ma covets after labour?

indicators.note: after labour suggests something worked over, so the letters of ma covets are reworked
final bit of takes the last letter of surgery

explanation.surface: A mother who has just given birth wants her partner to have one last operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after labour' rearranges MA COVETS into VASECTOM, and the final letter of 'surgery' completes it at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: This sterilising operation for men is a last procedure a weary new mother might want for her partner once she has had enough children.

clue.text: Oil, if freely flowing, makes everything very easy

indicators.note: flowing means running loose, so the letters of oil, if freely move into a new order

explanation.surface: Oil flowing freely keeps the machine running smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely flowing' reads as one phrase, but 'freely' is part of the fodder and 'flowing' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a carefree, comfortable existence in which nothing is a struggle.

clue.text: Car good for short journeys, no good for beach

indicators.note: no good means the good abbreviation is dropped

parts.note: to beach a boat is to run it aground

explanation.surface: A little car suits short trips but is useless on the sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no good for beach' sounds like a verdict on the car, but 'beach' is a verb: to drive a boat onto the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: A small car used for errands and local trips is often called by this name.

clue.text: May's purge requiring cabinet shuffling? Well, quite

parts.note: a spring is a natural well, a source of water
clean means quite or completely, as in clean forgot

explanation.surface: Theresa May clears out her ministers with a cabinet reshuffle, and quite right too.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was British Prime Minister in 2016 to 2019 and reshuffled her Cabinet; the clue also reads May as the month, when cupboards get turned out.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough clear-out of a house in springtime, such as in May, involves turning out cupboards and cabinets.

clue.text: One escaping English stuffiness cuts free, going topless

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so English stuffiness goes into the other word
topless takes away the top letter, the first of a down word

parts.note: a fug is a stuffy, smoky atmosphere

explanation.surface: Someone fleeing a stuffy English room breaks free and strips off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' takes the first letter from FREE to leave REE, into which E and FUG cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A refugee is a person fleeing war or persecution in their homeland.

clue.text: Reversing memory damage

indicators.note: reversing means running backwards, so the memory's letters are read from the end

parts.note: RAM is computer memory

explanation.surface: Backing a car into something can harm a person's memory.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to spoil or harm it.

clue.text: Wednesday turning somewhat dark, women scream

indicators.note: turning means turning round, so the letters of the dark word go backwards

parts.note: dim means fairly dark
eek is a cry of fright

explanation.surface: On a Wednesday the sky goes dark and women shriek.
explanation.definitionFit: Wednesday falls in the centre of the working week.

clue.text: A fair demeanour returns after cold nosh here

indicators.note: after means the rest follows the cold abbreviation

parts.note: a fete is a fair or fete day

indicators.note: returns means comes back, so the letters of demeanour run backwards

parts.note: an air is a manner or demeanour

explanation.surface: A cheerful manner comes back after a cold meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nosh' is British slang for food, and the definition reads as a place where food is eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service restaurant is a place where one eats a meal.

clue.text: One in jazz group, with two more

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one goes inside jazz

parts.note: trad is traditional jazz
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A single musician in a jazz combo is joined by two more players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' looks like part of the definition, but it is I, and 'group with two more' means a set of three.
explanation.definitionFit: A triad is a set of three, one member plus two others.

clue.text: Condition of faller at Becher's Brook, say

definitions.meaning: a clause added to a contract or bill, a proviso
a jockey thrown at the famous fence

explanation.surface: The state of a jockey who has come off at a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: Becher's Brook is a notorious fence in the Grand National, the British steeplechase, where many horses and jockeys fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is both an extra condition attached to a document and a jockey riding a horse.

clue.text: Why more said to be upset with large capacity?

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means turned upside down, read from the bottom
said means spoken, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: said aloud, the two words sound like the letter Y and a moor

explanation.surface: Someone asks why more people ought to be upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'Why more' gives Y + MOOR; 'to be upset' then flips that to read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere roomy has plenty of space inside.

clue.text: Running just after I admitted to clanger?

parts.note: on means immediately after, as in on arrival

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside, so the letter goes into the clanger

parts.note: a gong is something that clangs

explanation.surface: Straight after a blunder someone owns up to a clanger.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'clanger' is British slang for a blunder, but the question mark flags its literal reading: a thing that clangs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ongoing means continuing or in progress, as a project still running.

clue.text: Sentimentality of last character abandoning Mediterranean island

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving, so the last letter leaves the island

parts.note: Gozo is an island of Malta
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A soppy tale of a final resident deserting a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Goo is a slang word for cloying, mushy feeling.

clue.text: Where tiny person is guarded by minute Rottweiler

indicators.note: guarded by means held within, so the letters lie inside the dog's phrase

explanation.surface: A tiny person is protected by a little Rottweiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' wants to be the small dog's size, but it is just part of the text holding the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby before birth is inside the womb, which is what the Latin phrase means.

clue.text: Give last bits of rubbery scampi one final prod

indicators.note: the last bits of the words are their final letters, taken from each in turn

explanation.surface: Rubbery scampi finally yield to one last prod with the fork.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give way under pressure.

clue.text: Consent essential following Love Island party

indicators.note: following means the essential word comes after the rest

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
a key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys
a do is a party
key means essential

explanation.surface: Consent is vital after a Love Island party.
explanation.walkthrough: Love Island is a British reality TV dating show; here it splits into O and KEY.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jokey way of saying all right, signalling agreement.
